intro: A fixed-size feature vector avoids storing a growing vocabulary, but hash collisions mix token contributions. Signed hashing can make opposing collisions cancel.
task: Map token occurrences into a bounded signed feature vector and inspect deterministic collisions.
requirements: tokens is a list or tuple of at most 10000 nonempty strings; buckets is an integer 1..100000. Token matching is case-sensitive.
For each token compute h=0 then h=(31*h+ord(character)) mod 2**32 for each Unicode code point. Use bucket=(h//2) mod buckets and sign=+1 for even h, -1 for odd h.
Return a float vector of bucket sums, adding one signed contribution per token occurrence. This specified teaching hash is deterministic, not a cryptographic or security hash.

Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, except where a stricter bound is stated. Booleans are not numeric parameters. Leave all caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Apply the modulus at every character
hints.body: Use the exact stated hash recurrence so results are stable across Python processes.

hints.title: Separate bucket and sign
hints.body: The parity bit supplies the sign while the remaining integer selects the bucket.

explanation: Hashing bounds feature memory independently of vocabulary size. The cost is collisions: different tokens may share a coordinate and become indistinguishable to a downstream linear model.

This lesson fixes the hash function to make every collision inspectable. Production choices can use better-distributed hashes; Python built-in hash is unsuitable for this deterministic contract because its string results may vary between processes.
